name: Europe, Middle East & Africa

work_culture.communication: Formal in Germany/France. Direct but polite in Nordics/Netherlands. Hierarchical titles matter in DACH.
work_culture.hierarchy: More formal than NA. Titles used. Consensus-building expected (Scandinavia, Netherlands).
work_culture.hours: 35-40 hour norm. Overtime compensated or time-off-in-lieu. German 'Feierabend' culture — work ends at work end.
work_culture.remote: Growing but slower than NA. Germany/France have right-to-disconnect laws. Cross-border hiring complex (tax/social security).
work_culture.diversity_focus: Gender quota for boards (Germany, France, Norway). Age discrimination focus. Less ethnicity-focused than NA.

managerial_authority.budget_thresholds: Department heads: €20K-€100K. Directors: €100K-€500K. VP+: €500K+. Works council may need to approve certain decisions.
managerial_authority.hiring_authority: Long process. Works council involvement (Germany). Notice period means delayed starts.
managerial_authority.termination: Very difficult in Germany/France/Netherlands. Severance formulas common. Social plans for mass layoffs. Works council must be consulted.

industry_context.saas: Berlin/London/Paris/Stockholm hubs. Slower enterprise adoption than US.
industry_context.fintech: London, Berlin, Stockholm, Amsterdam. PSD2 regulation. Stronger banking partnerships.
industry_context.healthcare: Public healthcare systems mean different go-to-market. Strong medtech in Germany/Switzerland.
industry_context.manufacturing: Germany industrial heartland. Industry 4.0 leadership. Strong unions (IG Metall).
industry_context.ecommerce: Different marketplaces. Cross-border EU commerce. VAT MOSS complexity.

tax_year: Calendar (Jan-Dec) / UK: Apr-Mar for corporation tax
